title: Lebanese Civil War
summary: Fifteen years of war from April 1975 between Lebanon's Maronite, Sunni, Shia, Druze and Palestinian forces, with Syrian and Israeli armies in the country for most of it and a multinational force for part. About a hundred and twenty thousand people were killed and a million displaced; Beirut was divided by a green line for the duration. The Taif agreement of 1989 ended it by adjusting the confessional division of offices that had helped cause it. Its most consequential product outlasted it: Hezbollah, formed in the Israeli occupation of the south after 1982, was the one militia that did not disarm.
